correctness.rationale: For each X=B,C,c the exact Pell identities reduce the k-consecutive square sum to (B_k Q_{s+4n}±k)/D. The gcd of all terms is the gcd of the base numerator and B_k H_s divided by D, where H_s=gcd_n(Q_{s+4n}-Q_s) equals 96 if s≡2 mod4 and 16 if s≡0 mod4, from strong divisibility of Pell numbers. At odd primes >=5 the gcd is min of valuations of k and B_k; the extra 3-adic factor occurs only for c at k≡3 mod6; 2-adic congruences modulo 16 yield precisely the factor 1/2 for B at even k. These steps establish G_C(k)=gcd(k,B_k), G_B(k)=d_k or d_k/2 by parity and G_c(k)=3d_k iff k≡3 mod6, all k>=1. Independent direct recurrence/window gcds for k<=100, n<=20 verify 300 finite tests, not the infinite-gcd argument.
residual_risks: Independent finite gcd tests only support, but do not establish, gcd over all starting indices.
The fourth cobalancing-number sequence remains outside the theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary Journal of Integer Sequences paper explicitly poses squared-window gcds of these four balancing-associated families as Question 30 and tabulates some factor-two/factor-three numerical ratios; it does not give the three unrestricted gcd(k,B_k) formulas as established theorems. The 2022 generalized Fibonacci-square result assumes a different recurrence coefficient. The new assertion is the three magnitude formulas and proof, not the earlier numerical patterns.
residual_risks: An unindexed more general Lucas-sequence gcd theorem may subsume these formulas.
The 2023 numerical factor-ratio patterns are earlier observations and are not novel.

value.rationale: It resolves three natural, explicitly posed cases of a published four-family gcd problem and reduces infinite-window arithmetic to the computable index invariant gcd(k,B_k). The unsolved cobalancing-number fourth family is excluded; the partial resolution has independent number-theoretic value.
